subject: R squared when endogenous outcome is dichotomous

messages.author: 87b0ed968e68c1a9
messages.subject: R squared when endogenous outcome is dichotomous
parts:
I am running a mediation model in lavaan with no latent variables where the endogenous variable is dichotomous, so I am using the DWLS estimator. Two questions:

What is the R-Squared value that is produced, as a logistic approach does not really have a direct R squared value?

I ran the equivalent model in PROCESS in SPSS, and got similar results, but different magnitudes of coefficients. Does this difference reflect differences in the approach and algorithms?

Thanks.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: R squared when endogenous outcome is dichotomous
parts: What is the R-Squared value that is produced, as a logistic approach does not really have a direct R squared value?

lavaan uses a probit rather than logit link, but it is essentially the McKelvey & Zavoina pseudo-R-squared value described here: https://stats.idre.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/faq/general/faq-what-are-pseudo-r-squareds/
I ran the equivalent model in PROCESS in SPSS, and got similar results, but different magnitudes of coefficients. Does this difference reflect differences in the approach and algorithms?

If your simultaneous SEM is not saturated, then it contains constraints not reflected in the individual univariate models fitted by PROCESS. Also, it sounds like you might have been using logistic regression, whereas lavaan uses probit regression.  You can read about differences in a textbook such as Agresti's Introduction to Categorical Data Analysis.
